mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates expanding supply capacity, which typically coincides with positive corporate earnings momentum and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index above their respective 12-month averages for three months signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which reduces real purchasing power and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which erodes corporate revenue prospects and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above its 12-month average for six months indicates a larger working-age population entering the labor market, which can increase wage pressure and reduce profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable but PAYEMS rises above 12-month moving average for six months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered periods, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising above its 12-month average for eight consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which depresses consumer spending and corporate sales, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS exceeds 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.
